decisions.reason: The candidate already requires Pinata IPFS storage, and accepting Lit Protocol gating does not change its storage provider, protocol, or removal option.
Lit Protocol controls ownership verification and decryption before display; it does not necessarily replace PDF.js as the rendering technology or change the read-only viewing mode.
The accepted proposal specifies that NFT metadata points to a gated viewer but does not change the certificate email, its contents, or its read-action destination.

Encryption and decryption through a gated viewer may conflict with an offline PDF download, but the accepted proposal does not explicitly remove the download or specify whether a verified holder may download a decrypted copy.
The Lit Protocol access decision does not direct any FAQ copy change.
The accepted ebook-gating architecture does not necessarily change any About-page copy.
NFT ownership verification for ebook access does not change code-based referral commission rules.
The source decision concerns protected ebook access and does not entail revisions to Mission-page content.
Lit Protocol gating applies to ebook ownership access, not fiat buyers' dashboard access to commissions, tickets, or prizes.
The ebook-gating provider and encrypted-viewer flow do not change Small Block prize mechanics.
Automatic NFT ownership verification for ebook access does not alter commission allocation when no referral code is supplied.
The decision to encrypt and gate the PDF does not change presentation of the book-cover image on the landing page.
